title: Information architecture exploration for security alerts
status_note: Reconstructed from an earlier design discussion. Only eight priority inputs and the four candidate structures are provided by that discussion. Trees, scenario paths and numerical fit scores below are authored examples; they are NOT measured user outcomes.
design_question: Should alerts, workflows, resources or correlated incidents organize the primary security investigation experience?

scope_and_context.primary_job: Prioritize urgent alerts, investigate evidence, and take controlled remediation action
scope_and_context.primary_beneficiary: Security analyst handling triage and investigation
scope_and_context.evidence_status: user task and personas inferred from the assignment context; needs observation
assumptions: Analysts frequently enter via an alerts queue
Analysts need non-linear pivots between alert and resource evidence
Reliability of incident correlation is unknown
hard_constraints: Authorization and auditability for remediation actions
Applicable privacy, security and accessibility requirements

relationships: Alert references one or more evidence items
Alert can affect one or more assets
Incident groups zero or more alerts when correlation is supported
Alert and incident can have owners and state transitions
Remediation actions must be authorized and auditable
unknowns: Real user terminology and information hierarchy

task_scenarios.goal: Identify the most urgent unresolved alert and its likely blast radius
Inspect alert evidence and pivot to related assets or events
Assign ownership, record decision and initiate remediation
task_scenarios.edge_case: Responder lacks permission for a destructive action

task_scenarios.goal: Find all alerts affecting that resource

rubric.weight_origin: User-supplied task priority overrides from prior security-alert concept review; not research defaults

efficiency.label: Efficiency
efficiency.definition: How directly a user reaches high-priority tasks across entry points

information_density.label: Information density
information_density.definition: Useful decision context available without overwhelming the user
information_density.rubric_5: Critical context simultaneously accessible and distinguishable

discoverability.label: Discoverability
discoverability.definition: How well the hierarchy and labels expose where functions live
discoverability.rubric_5: Clear, predictable paths for intended users

user_control.label: User control
user_control.definition: Nonlinear navigation, filtering, exploration and recovery freedom

guidance.label: Guidance
guidance.definition: Support for knowing the next appropriate action during the task
guidance.rubric_5: Clear, contextual guidance without excessive restriction

flexibility.label: Flexibility
flexibility.definition: Ability to support alternate jobs and future pivots in the task
flexibility.rubric_5: Multiple efficient paths with predictable structure

consistency.label: Consistency
consistency.definition: Stable recognizable entities, labels and navigation patterns

simplicity.label: Simplicity
simplicity.definition: Ease of understanding the organizational model, not raw screen sparseness
simplicity.rubric_0: Unclear grouping and high translation burden
simplicity.rubric_5: Comprehensible groups and predictable mental map

alternatives.name: Alert-centered / object-oriented
alternatives.organizing_principle: Individual alert is canonical entry object; actions and related context hang off the alert
alternatives.search_and_filters: Global alert search, severity/status/owner filters, asset drill-in

task_walkthroughs.investigate: Open alert deep link → inspect evidence → pivot to asset or linked alerts
task_walkthroughs.remediate: Alert detail → ownership and remediation panel → status
task_walkthroughs.asset: Asset detail → related alerts → alert detail

benefits: Strong fast triage and granular control
Preserves separate alert details and investigation pivots
failure_modes: Can fragment a single incident into many alerts
Analyst may manually synthesize context across related signals
First-time responders may lack workflow guidance
alternatives.fit_rationale: Hypothesis: a frequently used alert queue and detail object support high-volume triage and flexible pivots; guidance and correlation remain weaker.
unknown_constraints: Data-level authorization for linked assets must be specified

alternatives.name: Workflow / task-oriented
alternatives.organizing_principle: Users progress across explicit triage, investigation, remediation, and resolution stages
alternatives.search_and_filters: Stage-specific queues and task search with cross-stage history

task_walkthroughs.investigate: Direct link → determine stage → navigate investigation context
task_walkthroughs.remediate: Investigate → Remediate stage → review and assign
task_walkthroughs.asset: Asset search → choose stage-specific related alerts

benefits: May help unfamiliar analysts follow a standard process
failure_modes: Rigid stages hinder non-linear expert investigations
Same alert may appear in several stage contexts
Deep links may create ambiguous landing states
alternatives.fit_rationale: Hypothesis: stage grouping teaches process but adds navigation for analysts who need to pivot unpredictably.
unknown_constraints: Workflow stage boundaries and escalation rules need validation

alternatives.name: Resource / asset-oriented
alternatives.organizing_principle: Servers, cloud services and applications are the top-level information objects
alternatives.search_and_filters: Service ownership, environment and resource property filters

task_walkthroughs.investigate: Deep-linked alert → identify asset → resource timeline
task_walkthroughs.remediate: Resource → locate alert → owner and action

benefits: Natural for platform owners starting from a known service
failure_modes: Organization-wide alert queue harder to access
alternatives.fit_rationale: Hypothesis: effective for asset-centered users, worse when triage starts from an organization-wide alert priority.
unknown_constraints: Resource inventory coverage and owner mappings unknown

alternatives.name: Incident / correlation-oriented
alternatives.organizing_principle: Group related security signals into an incident-level investigation entity
navigation_tree: └─ Incident detail → Signals / Assets / Timeline / Response
alternatives.search_and_filters: Incident status, severity, related alerts, blast radius and owner filters

task_walkthroughs.triage: Incident queue → open correlated group → decide
task_walkthroughs.investigate: Alert deep link → incident → signals, evidence and assets

benefits: Groups noise into actionable cases when correlation is reliable
Presents related evidence and responders together
failure_modes: Incorrect correlation obscures critical standalone alerts
Users may distrust grouping and need raw-alert escape
Dependent on correlation quality and editorial rules
alternatives.fit_rationale: Hypothesis: strong when signals reliably group; limited without validated correlation and an accessible raw-alert view.
unknown_constraints: No evidence of signal correlation accuracy; must not suppress independent critical alerts

provisional_recommendation.overlay: Workflow cues for next actions, resource-based filtering/cross-links, contextual AI assistance (not a top-level IA destination)
provisional_recommendation.reason: High task weights on control, efficiency and information density provisionally favor an alert-level canonical object with flexible pivots. This is a hypothesis, not proof.
conditions_for_reversal: If reliable correlation demonstrably improves task success, test incident-first IA
If dominant jobs begin from a known asset, resource-first may win
If novice guided response is the priority, workflow-first may win
who_may_lose: Novice analysts who need process guidance
Incident responders dealing with many related alerts

known_evidence_gaps: No observed security analyst mental models or tree-test results
No directly measured time-to-triage, findability or remediation success
Option fit estimates assigned for demonstration, not user or stakeholder validated

before_wireframes: Task analysis across analyst and platform-owner roles
Tree test the four candidate navigation structures with representative tasks
Low-fidelity workflow walkthrough of deep-link, filtering, evidence pivot and remediation
Audit every architecture for security permissions and critical-alert visibility
metrics: Task success on triage and investigation
Recovery from missing or mis-grouped evidence
validation.invalidation: If incident-first or workflow-first consistently outperforms alert-first on priority tasks without harming critical alert access, revise the preferred IA.
